1.0.0.en: First release: your Homey dashboards in any browser, with browser pairing and kiosk mode.

1.0.1.en: Settings: explains that keys from my.homey.app need full access for dashboards, and how to make a narrower one.

1.1.0.en: New: a Fit to screen width option in the dashboard's Settings, and open dashboards reload by themselves after an app update. Fixed: the live camera's full-screen button now also exits full screen, zone device widgets set to all device types show their devices again, and app widgets can only reach their own API.

1.2.0.en: New: Flow cards to show a dashboard or highlight a widget large or full screen (the door camera when the bell rings, for example) on all screens or one named screen, check and close the highlight, and react when it closes. Screens are named in the app settings. Live cameras: widgets showing the same camera share one stream, so a second one shows video at once.

1.3.0.en: New: edit dashboards from the browser. Edit moves, edits and removes widgets, and a widget's settings work like in the Homey app: its title, devices and its app's own settings. App widgets that need storage can get it while staying sealed off from the API key, or be trusted to run as in the Homey app. Editing needs a key with the Dashboards permission (homey.dashboard). Fixed: app widgets sized as a share of their width are no longer cut off, and popups from app widgets can no longer reach the dashboard's stored key.

1.3.1.en: Fixed: on a Homey Self-Hosted Server, Open dashboard and Copy link now use its own https port, and device tiles have the same gap as the other widgets.

1.4.1.en: Dashboard workspace inside Homey with desktop dashboard navigation. Automatic Homey connection replaces manual key setup for new screens; separate displays connect with one approval. Shared native dashboard edits remain available in the mobile apps.

1.4.0.en: New: edit mode now also changes built-in widgets: the devices, lights, speaker, thermostat, Flows, moods, variables or dashboards a widget shows, a note's colour, a line chart's Insight, time span and dark mode, and the categories a Timeline shows. Fixed: a Timeline leaves out the categories switched off in the Homey app, a chart set to dark mode stays dark, and a light widget shows its own name.

1.4.2.en: The integrated workspace uses the working Homey settings address on your local network, including self-hosted servers whose generated secure hostname cannot be resolved.

1.4.3.en: Automatic connection also works when the browser omits the embedded dashboard referrer, after verifying the same-origin Homey app settings page.

1.4.4.en: Homey web app settings now connect through a private per-visit channel, supporting Homey’s restricted app frames without browser API credentials or manual setup.

1.4.5.en: Automatic connections include Homey’s SDK identity header for local API requests. Refused requests show a concise reason with backend credentials removed.

1.4.6.en: Native dashboard connections can use a dedicated scoped key held only on Homey when firmware restricts the built-in app credential. Connection status checks the actual dashboard grant; a rejected configured key never silently falls back to another credential.

1.4.7.en: Reload creates a new embedded page and private connection instead of changing only its fragment, so a failed connection can start again correctly.

1.4.8.en: The embedded page receives Homey’s authorization failure immediately, preserving the useful reason instead of replacing it with a later generic connection timeout.

1.5.0.en: Desktop companion adds Dashboards to the main navigation of the local Homey web app and opens a full-width workspace. Hosted views retain normal browser pairing and pause live cameras and updates while hidden.

1.5.1.en: Live cameras keep one connection across duplicate visibility notifications and cancel obsolete connection attempts cleanly. A camera that sends no video shows a bounded retry message. Resuming after an event-subscription gap reloads current Homey data instead of leaving an older dashboard visible.

1.5.2.en: Camera connection requests have a dedicated startup window so cold cameras are not cut off by the shorter ordinary-control limit. The embedded Homey view uses matching bounded deadlines and reports camera timeouts accurately. Other request limits, permissions and playback preferences stay the same.
